details: At the July 2026 Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, three officials dissented from the majority, advocating for a 25 basis point interest rate hike instead of maintaining the current 3.50%-3.75% federal funds target range. This hawkish split signals ongoing concerns about inflation remaining elevated and creates uncertainty for future monetary policy, potentially impacting crypto market liquidity. New York Fed President John Williams indicated that the Fed would not hesitate to raise rates if inflation doesn't ease.
title: Three Fed Officials Voted for Rate Hike Amid Persistent Inflation Fears

details: The Digital Asset Market CLARITY Act, a key piece of US legislation aimed at establishing clear regulatory frameworks for cryptocurrencies, continues to face delays in the Senate. This prolonged regulatory uncertainty is discouraging institutional investors and keeping significant capital on the sidelines, contributing to thinner market liquidity and suppressed cryptocurrency prices, in contrast to Europe's fully implemented MiCA regulations.
title: US CLARITY Act Delays Keep Crypto Institutional Capital Sidelined

details: Bitcoin has entered August, a month that has historically seen negative returns for the past four consecutive years. Currently trading around $63,000, the cryptocurrency is also encountering a substantial $1.17 billion "put wall" at the $60,000 strike price on Deribit. This concentration of put options could serve as a critical support level, but a breach could accelerate downward price movement.
title: Bitcoin Faces "Worst Month" Historically with $60K Put Wall in August

details: Reports of diplomatic progress between the US and Iran, including a pause in US strikes, have led to a de-escalation of geopolitical tensions in the Middle East. This development has contributed to a sharp decline in oil prices and an overall improvement in global risk appetite, providing temporary support for riskier assets, including the cryptocurrency market.
title: US-Iran Diplomatic Progress Calms Oil Markets, Aids Risk Assets

details: A security vulnerability in Coldcard hardware wallets, stemming from a firmware update in March 2021 that utilized a weak pseudo-random number generator, has resulted in approximately $88.6 million in Bitcoin being stolen across 4,585 addresses. The exploit allowed attackers to reconstruct private keys. While not directly impacting Bitcoin's price significantly, this incident raises concerns about the security of self-custody solutions.
title: Coldcard Wallet Exploit Causes $88.6 Million in Bitcoin Losses
